lines: Four channel utility mixer with panning into a stereo output, each channel built on a different gain stage
Sets the amplitude of the stereo outputs
Sets the depth of modulation from the level CV input
Places that channel across the stereo output, on an equal loudness contour
Attenuates channel one's input, on an audio taper
Scales whatever reaches channel two's CV input, which is a +6V reference while nothing is patched there, so it works as a level control
Produces the offset that sums with channel three's modulator input, on an audio taper, over the range set by the polarity switch
Crossfades between channel four's two inputs, on a linear taper
Sets the range of channel three's fader offset, bipolar on one side and unipolar positive on the other
Modulates the stereo output level, scaled by its attenuator and summed with the LEVEL knob
Moves channel one across the stereo field, summed with its pan knob
The modulator for channel two's two quadrant VCA, scaled by that channel's fader; unpatched it holds a +6V reference
The modulator for channel three's four quadrant VCA, summed with that channel's fader
The second signal into channel four's crossfader
The signal into that channel
The first signal into channel four's crossfader
The right side of the stereo mix, summed after the faders and pans
The left side of the stereo mix, summed after the faders and pans
That channel alone, taken after its fader and before its pan
Menu — Limiter: Off, On — runs the stereo outputs through a soft clipping stage
Menu — Output Normalisation: Half, Full — one per channel, under that channel's heading: Half takes that channel out of the stereo mix once its own output is patched, Full leaves it in
Menu — Input Coupling: AC, DC — one per channel, under that channel's heading: AC strips DC offsets from that channel for audio, DC keeps them for control voltage
Menu — Allow Chaining — sums the stereo mix into a càrn or a cuïr immediately to the right, and takes in the mix of a càrn on the left, in place of the hardware's back panel stereo jacks
carn.notes: Instruo 2.2.0 binary: Carn::onExpanderChange tests the left neighbour against modelCarn and the right neighbour against modelCarn or modelCuir, and Carn::process adds the left neighbour's message to the mix and writes the mix to the right one, so the chain runs left to right and ends at a cuïr.
